# RawiBumi design system

RawiBumi is an engineering workstation used for whole working days. Light stone panels sit around a warm graphite drawing workspace. Colour carries meaning, never decoration. The drawing itself, with real dimensions, ISO 3098 lettering and IEC symbols, is the product's signature.

Read this file before changing anything visible. Tokens live in `src/ui/tokens.json`. The front matter above and `src/ui/tokens.css` are generated from it with `npm run gen:tokens`.

Status: F8 candidate (22 Oct 2026), based on F7.1. Accessibility and recovery hardening are recorded in ADR 0017. Gate F still requires the engineer usability sessions and the outstanding engine evidence in `docs/F8_QC.md`.

## 1. Surfaces

| Surface | Token | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Stone, shell | `--rb-role-shell-bg` (stone 200) | Header, rail, status bar |
| Stone, panels | `--rb-role-panel-bg` (stone 100) | Task panel, inspector, full-width views |
| Stone, raised | `--rb-role-panel-raised` (stone 50) | Inputs, cards, dialogs, the command palette |
| Graphite | `--rb-role-stage-bg`, `--rb-role-stage-surface`, `--rb-role-stage-grid` | The plan, 3D and SLD stage only |
| Paper | `--rb-color-paper-*` | Report pages and exported figures |

Rules:

- Panels are light, the stage is dark. Never put a dark panel inside the stone chrome, or a light card on the stage.
- Control borders use `--rb-role-control-border` (stone 500, 3:1 or more on every stone). Stone 300 and 400 are for dividers only.
- Text on stone uses `--rb-role-panel-text`; text on graphite uses `--rb-role-stage-text`.
- The workspace grid is the solar-cell grid (`--rb-role-stage-grid`). It also forms the empty state. It is not used anywhere else.

## 2. Colour roles

| Role | Token | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Selection, active step | `--rb-role-selection` (#FFB238) | The only use of the sun palette inside the app. Text version on stone: `--rb-role-selection-text` |
| Warning | glyph `--rb-role-warning-glyph`, text `--rb-role-warning-text` | Always glyph plus text, never colour alone |
| Error / blocked | glyph `--rb-role-error-glyph`, text `--rb-role-error-text` | Same |
| Valid | `--rb-role-valid` | Same |
| Links, focus, info | `--rb-role-link`, `--rb-role-focus`, `--rb-role-info-on-stage` | TSE blue |
| MPPT groups | `--rb-color-mppt-screen-1..8`, paper `--rb-color-mppt-paper-1..8` | Cool hues only. Unassigned modules are hatched, not coloured |
| Heatmaps | Inferno ramp | Sequential data only |

#FABC3C and #FF773D belong to the logo only.

Known limit: on stone, the sun glyphs are below the 3:1 contrast WCAG 1.4.11 asks of graphical objects. #FFB238 is 1.6:1 and #F19143 is 2.2:1. On graphite all three glyph colours pass.

Decided in F1 (ADR 0008): keep the brand hues, and never let a sun glyph carry meaning alone on stone.

- Warnings always pair the glyph with text.
- The active rail step is also bold and on a lighter row.
- The rail's diamond marker gets a 1 px outline in `--rb-role-selection-text`.

## 3. Typography

| Role | Token | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Interface | `--rb-font-ui` | 13 px body and controls, 15 px section, 20 px page title |
| Dense tables | `--rb-font-ui-narrow` | 12 px, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, numbers right-aligned |
| IDs | `--rb-font-mono` | INV-02, MPPT-2, S-07 only |
| Wordmark | `--rb-font-wordmark` | The RAWIBUMI wordmark only |
| Drawing and SLD | `--rb-font-drawing` (osifont) | Dimensions, labels, string IDs, SLD |

The interface font is Archivo, with Archivo Narrow for dense tables (ADR 0011). Sentence case everywhere, including buttons and headings. Units follow the number with a non-breaking space: `12.00 m`, `540 Wp`, `1,411.2 MWh`.

## 4. Layout and density

- Regions: header, rail (196 px, or 56 px compact), task panel, stage, inspector, and status bar with the quantities. Typed input appears at the cursor while a plan tool is active (ADR 0012).
- The stage gets the room: the task panel and the inspector collapse to a 32 px strip (`Alt+[` and `Alt+]`), and Focus (`Alt+\`) collapses both and compacts the rail. At 1440 px the stage goes from 632 px to 1,318 px. In the electrical step a resizable bottom panel under the stage holds the string table (F5).
- Spacing: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32 px only.
- Radius: 2–4 px for controls and 8 px at most anywhere. Borders: 1 px.
- Shadows only on floating menus and dialogs: at most `0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12)`.
- Property grids may be denser than the detector's padding rule. That is intentional for CAD and recorded in the quality baseline.

## 5. Components

- **Buttons:** solid fill or 1 px border, 4 px radius, 28–32 px tall in panels. One primary action per region.
- **Pane strip:** a collapsed task panel or inspector is a 32 px strip on the shell colour, with an expand icon and the pane name set vertically. The whole strip is the button.
- **Collapsible section:** a chevron and the title; when closed it may show a one-line summary in the narrow face. Long repeated groups (inverters) get Expand all / Collapse all and start closed from three up.
- **Rail item:** a two-digit step number, the label, a small rotated-square marker on the active step, and a status glyph (valid, warning or blocked) with hidden text for screen readers. The active step is bold on the panel colour. No left-border tab, no round numbered markers.
- **Header:** mark and wordmark, project, revision and time zone in mono, then undo, redo, commands (Ctrl/⌘ K), projects, and one primary button (save).
- **Status bar:** quantities on the left (modules, DC kWp, strings, unassigned, DC/AC); findings counts with glyphs on the right. They open the findings list above the bar.
- **Command palette:** every command, with its keys. Shortcuts and the shortcut sheet (Shift+?) read the same command list.
- **Tables:** 1 px rules and no zebra stripes. Sticky header. Virtualised above 200 rows.
- **Findings:** a glyph, a one-line message and a "why" link to the inspector. Nothing is auto-fixed.
- **Preview state:** shown as "Preview, not applied yet", with Apply and Discard. Applying is a single undo step.
- **Recovery and dialogs (F8):** native modal focus with a visible TSE-blue ring, Tab wrap, Escape and focus return. The file input stays keyboard-reachable. Loading, unavailable and empty states differ; failed creation preserves the form and focuses its inline error. Errors remain until dismissed. Error text is dark enough for the shell as well as raised panels.
- **Empty state:** the cell grid with one line and the keyboard shortcut ("Draw the first roof. Press P and click its corners.").

## 6. Drawing grammar (stage, report figures, SLD)

- **Lettering:** osifont for all drawing text, sized in metres on the plan.
- **Dimensions:** thin lines with ticks, the value centred above, two decimals in metres.
- **Modules:** MPPT fill at 0.75 opacity with a 1 px outline in the same hue (drawn once a module is about 7 px wide). Unassigned modules get a 45° hatch at 8 px pitch. Outside the electrical step, modules are the module colour at 0.55 opacity.
- **Strings:** a polyline in wiring order, + at the start, – at the end (en dash; osifont has no U+2212), and the ID in mono at the start.
- **Inverters:** an IEC symbol placed on the plan, with a dashed hull around the modules it serves.
- **Selection:** a 2 px outline in the selection colour. Never recolour the fill. (A module too small on screen for an outline is filled with the selection colour so it stays visible.)
- **Layers (plan):** Canvas 2D base (underlay, grid), WebGL geometry (surfaces, keep-outs, modules, obstacles), Canvas 2D overlay (lettering, selection, handles, previews). Lettering is screen-sized and stays on the overlay (ADR 0010).
- **PV layout overlay (F4):** the usable region after setbacks is a dashed outline in the info colour. Preview modules are the valid colour at 0.28 opacity with a 1 px outline, and are labelled "Preview, not applied". Tables a re-fill would remove are dimmed, with a dashed red outline. Table outlines show from about 3 px per metre. A pinned table has a pin mark at its front-left corner and an info-coloured outline. A deleted, pinned table is a dashed muted outline labelled "removed (pinned)".
- **Electrical overlay (F5):** each string is a polyline through its modules in wiring order, in its MPPT colour (muted when unassigned), from about 4 px per metre; + marks the first module and – the last. From about 10 px per metre the string id sits at its + end with the worst live check as a glyph (red circle with ! for fail, amber triangle for warn). The string path being drawn is the selection colour with numbered stops; the lasso is a dashed selection-colour loop at 0.12 fill.
- **Results charts (F7):**
  - Paper roles on the stone results page: series in `role-chart-1`, `role-chart-2`, then the paper MPPT hues; losses in `role-chart-loss`; 1 px `role-chart-grid` lines; no animation.
  - The heatmap uses the heat ramp (sequential data only), and its caption states the hours shown and left out.
  - Demo series carry the dashed "Demo data" stamp.
- **Report (F7):**
  - A4, Archivo on paper white, chapter numbers in mono.
  - The plan figure keeps the graphite stage, framed; the SLD is drawn in paper ink.
  - Tables use 1 px rules with tabular figures.
  - A synthetic run carries the orange "Demo data" stamp under the title.
- **3D preview:** graphite massing lit softly from the south-west; labelled "Preview" until the engine's 3D scene is wired.
- **North arrow and scale bar** always visible on the plan and in report figures.
- **SLD (F6):** generated from the assignment, left to right: strings → MPPT inputs → inverter → AC busbar → grid, load below.
  - Symbols are the in-house IEC 60617 set (`src/electrical/symbols/`), drawn as 1.4 px outlines in the stage text colour; the busbar is 4 px.
  - Lettering is osifont with a stage-coloured halo: string id and module count at the left, Vmp below, MPPT and inverter labels above.
  - A selected node gets a 2 px selection-colour box, dashed when only some of its modules are selected.
  - Live-check glyphs sit at a string's top right, as on the plan.
  - Muted (55 % opacity): an MPPT with no strings, or a string with no MPPT.
  - The symbol sheet lists every symbol with its terminals as dots.

## 7. Motion

100–200 ms opacity or colour changes only (`--rb-motion-*`). No bounce, no slide-ins, no scroll-triggered animation. Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## 8. Copy

Plain engineering English, with Bahasa Indonesia from F1. Active voice ("Assign 7 modules to MPPT-2"). Errors say what to do next. No marketing words, no exclamation marks, no emoji. Never call a demo number a result.

## 9. Do and don't

Do:

- Show the engine's findings verbatim, with the rule ID available on hover.
- Give every mouse action a typed equivalent and a key. Typed points: `x,y`, `@dx,dy`, `d<bearing` (0° = north, clockwise) or a distance along the cursor; values take arithmetic and `m`, `cm` or `mm`.
- Keep the selection identical across plan, tree, SLD and inspector.

Don't:

- Pills, glass or frosted panels, glows, gradient fills, coloured shadows.
- KPI-card grids, hero blocks, eyebrow labels or uppercase micro-labels.
- Left-border accent tabs, or radius above 8 px.
- Lucide or a second icon set (Tabler plus in-house PV icons only).
- Inter, Roboto or Arial as the primary face.
- Recomputing engineering values in the browser, except previews labelled as such.
